s: concrete, objective (representative or involving the physical, perceivable or real; not abstract)
concrete, specific (tangibly applicable or measurable in the situation at hand; not general)
konkret.et: Borrowed from Latin concrētus, past participle of concrescere (com- + crescere).

s: Was geht? Was geht? / Ich sag's dir ganz konkret
What's up? What's up? / I'll tell you in concrete terms
konkret.et: Borrowed from Latin concrētus, past participle of concrescere (com- + crescere).

s: to concrete; to solidify (of ideas, proposals, plans, etc.)
Die Produkte der Konkurrenz mögen ähnlich sein, aber sie haben nicht die gleiche Qualität.

Konkurrenz.et: From Latin concurrentia (“concurrence; competition”). Compare English concurrence.

Konkurs.et: From Latin concursus + creditorum (assembly of creditors)

konkurrieren.et: From Latin concurrō (“run with”) + -ieren. Cognate with English concur.

Konklave.et: Early 15th century, borrowed from Latin conclāve n.

konkordant.et: From Latin concordans, present participle of concordare (“to agree”), from con- + cor (“heart”).

s: concordat (formal agreement between a nation and the Vatican)
Formal agreement between a nation's federal government and its subdivisions, e.g. states or cantons.
Konkordat.et: From Medieval Latin concordatum, from Latin concordāre (“to agree”).
